chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him),

he said: The hearts are three: a heart that is inverted, which does not grasp any good, and this is the heart of the disbeliever; and a heart in which there is a black spot, so good and evil contend within it, and whichever is stronger overcomes it; and an open heart in which there is a lamp that shines and its light is not extinguished until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the heart of the believer.

key_terms.نَكْتَةٌ سَوَاءُ: Black spot (indicating a mix of faith and disbelief)
key_terms.يَعْتَلِجَانِ: Contend or struggle against each other

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of hearts described in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes human hearts into three types based on their spiritual state: the heart of the disbeliever which is closed to good, the heart of the hypocrite or mixed believer where good and evil struggle, and the heart of the true believer which is open and illuminated with enduring light. This tripartite classification reflects the Shia theological understanding of *fitrah* and spiritual receptivity, highlighting the dynamic nature of the believer's heart as a vessel of divine light that remains unextinguished until the Day of Judgment. The narration serves as a practical guide for self-reflection, encouraging believers to cultivate an 'open' heart receptive to divine guidance while guarding against the stagnation of the 'closed' heart.

en.basel-kadem: 49.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Qasem bin Muhammed al-Esbahani, from Sulayman bin Dawud al-Manqari, from Sufyan bin ‘Uyayna, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:

I have the knowledge of people, all of them, in four: the first is that you know your Lord; the second is that you know what He has done to you; the third is that you know what He wants from you; and the fourth is that you know that which makes you leave your religion.
